summary: This note is a wiki-style article on the Houston Astros, an MLB team based in Houston, Texas, that moved from the National League to the American League West in 2013 after 51 seasons in the NL. It covers the 2011 announcement of the move under owner Jim Crane, the franchise's history of division titles and pennants, and its 2017 championship run, which was the first World Series title in franchise history. It also includes team infobox data such as nicknames, ballparks, titles, and front office personnel.
one_line: The Houston Astros are an MLB team in Houston, Texas, who moved from the National League to the American League West in 2013 and won the 2017 World Series.
key_facts: On November 15, 2011, it was announced that Crane had agreed to move the Astros franchise to the American League for the 2013 season.
Crane was given a $70 million concession by MLB for agreeing to the switch to the American League.
The Astros were officially sold to Jim Crane two days after the move announcement, after the other owners unanimously voted in favor of the sale.
The Astros played in the National League from 1962 to 2012, spending their first 51 seasons in the NL before moving to the AL in 2013.
The Astros have played their home games at Minute Maid Park since 2000.
In 2017 the Astros won their first AL West division title as an American League member and became the first team in Major League history to win three different divisions.
On September 29, 2017, the Astros won their 100th game of the season, finishing 101-61 with a 21-game division lead.
The Astros defeated the Boston Red Sox three games to one in the AL Division Series, then beat the New York Yankees four games to three in the ALCS.
The Astros defeated the Los Angeles Dodgers in the deciding seventh game of the 2017 World Series, winning the first championship in franchise history.
In 2017 the Astros became the first franchise in MLB history to have won a pennant in both the NL and the AL.
While in the NL, the Astros played in one World Series, in 2005, and were swept in four games by the Chicago White Sox.
The Astros' team colors are navy blue, orange, and white, and the franchise has 10 retired numbers.
Jeff Luhnow was the general manager, A.J. Hinch the manager, and Reid Ryan the president of baseball operations in the front office listed in the note.
